items.title: Appeals court tosses methodology for calculating NSA qualifying payment amounts
items.reason: This article directly addresses federal litigation that challenges the methodology for calculating qualifying payment amounts under the No Surprises Act, which is core to the IDR process and balance-billing protections.
items.summary: A federal appeals court has invalidated the methodology used to calculate qualifying payment amounts in No Surprises Act out-of-network claim disputes. This ruling affects how the Independent Dispute Resolution process determines payment benchmarks, which is central to resolving surprise billing disputes and protecting patients from balance-bill liability. The decision creates immediate uncertainty for healthcare providers and payers operating under the existing NSA framework, potentially requiring CMS to establish new calculation methods or allowing litigation to proceed on the underlying methodological issues.
